text:
The stock rose slightly today while oil prices fell sharply—US crude dropped to $89.53 and global oil to $92.94—which is typical weakness for an energy major. But the move was muted because geopolitical tension in the Middle East has rattled the market; Iran's escalating attacks on US and allied installations in the Gulf over the past two days have made traders nervous about Strait of Hormuz shipping and supply disruptions, which typically supports oil prices and energy stocks even when broader crude weakness prevails.

The stock has fallen hard over the past week (down $5.60 from $140 to $135), tracking a sharp pullback in oil prices that began around the 18th. This suggests the geopolitical risk premium hasn't been enough to offset the weight of weakening crude demand or supply concerns—possibly tied to softer global growth expectations rather than any structural change in Middle Eastern conflict risk.
